rationale: Record Pulp-owned retained-layout work that extends the anonymous flex item to a container whose text has no element siblings. build_yoga_subtree previously attached the text measure func to the Label's own node whenever that Label had no managed children, which made the Label a Yoga leaf: justify-content and align-items had no item on the line to distribute, and the text was painted at the content-box origin on both axes regardless of the container's alignment. The same anonymous measure-func child already synthesized for a Label that carries text alongside element children is now also synthesized when the text is alone, so layout writes the Label's own text box and the existing paint path honors it. The gate is narrow by construction: alignment that cannot displace a lone item -- justify-content flex-start or space-between, align-items stretch or flex-start -- does not qualify, so a plain text-only Label builds the identical tree it built before; and a Label carrying browser-captured line boxes is excluded outright, because those rectangles are recorded relative to the owning element's content box and already encode the distribution the browser resolved, so resolving it again would offset each line by the sum of both. The anonymous item also carries CSS's initial shrink factor of one, so a long string compresses inside a fixed-width container rather than overflowing it as a fresh Yoga node's zero shrink factor would allow. Touched at core/view/src/yoga_layout.cpp, at the tests that pin it, and at the compat matrix row for css/justifyContent, which now states that the property distributes a container's own bare text and names the captured-line-box exception. No public signature, no measure-func contract, and no child-ordering rule outside the synthesized node changes. This is Pulp-only. The anonymous-inline-box rule it encodes is generic CSS behaviour and a Vellum-native retained UI will need an equivalent, but it should derive one from its own text-ownership model rather than copy Pulp's Label-typed dynamic_cast and clear_own_text_box handshake, which exist because Pulp stores a container's text on the container itself. There is no named immutable Vellum framework commit to backport against, and this records no Vellum acknowledgement: no design ingest, captured output, packaging behavior, accepted expansion boundary, or Vellum source authority changes.
